why: On SpaceX's Oct 20 Q3 call, Musk said the Tesla and SpaceX boards have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger. He called it a good idea but said no terms are agreed and there's no guarantee (CNBC, BBC, WSJ, FT).

Oct 21: SpaceX's 8-K is its earnings release with no Tesla merger language. Wednesday's coverage (NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg, Fox Business) recapped the committee news; Reuters added, citing a person familiar, that Tesla is working with an investment bank and the deal could take the form of SpaceX acquiring Tesla. That fits the committee signal already counted, so no change.
The Dec 3 meeting is still routine, so a deal goes through a separate announcement, an S-4 and a 2027 special meeting. Tesla needs 50% of all outstanding shares, which Musk called a high hurdle.

Tesla's Q3 results came out Oct 21 with no merger language in the 8-K or shareholder deck, and on the call Musk said only that he'd said everything that should be said the day before. Evening coverage (WSJ, NYT, FT, Yahoo Finance) recaps the committee news, so no change. SpaceX's 1.3B-share unlock is Thursday Oct 22.

Oct 22: Reuters (a person with direct knowledge) says Musk's public endorsement rattled insiders and could delay the process by several weeks; talks are early, advisers are hired, and structures include SpaceX buying Tesla or a new holding company. Bloomberg (people familiar) says an announcement is targeted for the first half of 2027. Neither changes whether a deal happens, but both push it later, so the rules model moved weight from late 2026 into early 2027. Dec 31, 2026 odds fell from 18.0% to 13.4%; Jun 30, 2027 is about unchanged at 55.9%. Kalshi's May 1, 2027 contract dropped from 64.5% to 48% overnight on a thin quote.

Oct 22 morning: Tesla's Q3 10-Q formally confirms the board formed a special committee of disinterested directors to explore deepening the relationship with SpaceX, including a possible business combination, subject to the committee's recommendation and shareholder approval. That's already counted, so no change. The headline is 12.7% for a merger letter by Dec 31, 2026 and 56.1% by Jun 30, 2027; Polymarket's Dec 31 contract slipped to 16%.

Oct 22 evening: SpaceX's Q3 10-Q formally confirms its board also formed a special committee of independent directors to explore a possible combination with Tesla, and says any deal would need approval from Musk as SpaceX's controlling stockholder. That was expected and the committees are already counted, so no change.

Nov 6 evening: SpaceX 8-K (Item 5.02) — Donald Harrison (Google; independent Class B director) resigned effective Nov 4; filing says no disagreement; Google says still supportive. Tesla DEFA14A is another routine VoteTesla letter for the Dec 3 meeting with no merger language. Neither changes committees, structure, or timeline, so no news nudge.

Nov 12, 3:09 PM ET: Bloomberg (people familiar) says SpaceX-Tesla merger talks are progressing; boards and advisers are working through terms, governance and the share exchange, and a deal could be announced as soon as December but could slip into 2027. Open hurdles: Tesla's China operations, SpaceX's US defense ties, and shareholder and regulatory approval. That is the first sign since Oct 22 that talks are moving faster, so the rules model shifted weight back into December and raised total letter odds by Jun 30, 2027 from 56% to 60%. Prediction markets jumped on the report (Polymarket and Kalshi Dec 31 contracts), which flows into the blend automatically.

Nov 13 morning: overnight coverage only echoed Bloomberg's talks report; Texas AG-elect Nathan Johnson's vow to scrutinize any SpaceX-Tesla merger is political risk for 2027 approvals, not a sign of timing, so no change. No new filings. The headline is 21.0% for a merger letter by Dec 31, 2026 (rules 13.0%, markets 32.9%) and 64.2% by Jun 30, 2027.

Starship Flight 15 was scored a success after the first Ship tower catch from orbit on Nov 14; that is a calendar input, not merger news. The only new filing was a passive SpaceX 13G/A on Nov 13. The Nov 15 recalibration changed the method, not the facts. The headline is 20.3% for a merger letter by Dec 31, 2026 (rules 13.7%, markets 27.0%) and 69.2% by Jun 30, 2027, moved since Friday by markets and the recalibration only.
